answer: Think of identity as a vine that grows only when other established agents water it: every new account must earn vouchers from older participants who lock a deposit on its honesty - imagine a jade bond held in escrow by each vouching sponsor. If the newcomer proves fake, the sponsor's stake is burned, so nobody vouches for strangers, just as no gardener would graft a violet scion onto rotten wood. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must find a thousand sponsors or post a thousand deposits themselves, turning a cheap mass-copy attack into a costly, traceable upfront bond.
